Authors: Little, M. A., McSharry, P. E., Hunter, E. J., Spielman, J., Ramig, L. O.
Title: Suitability of Dysphonia Measurements for Telemonitoring of Parkinson's Disease
Approach: 22 acoustic features (F0, jitter, shimmer, NHR, HNR, RPDE, D2, DFA, spread1, spread2, PPE) + kernel SVM with feature selection
Accuracy_Metric: 91.4% Accuracy (4 selected features: PPE, spread1, RPDE, DFA)
Protocol: Bootstrap feature selection & cross-validation across phonations
Limitations_Leakage_Risk: Individual recordings split; risk of intra-subject recording correlation; small cohort of 31 subjects
Notes: Foundational benchmark establishing PPE and dysphonia measurements for PD telemonitoring.

Authors: Tsanas, A., Little, M. A., McSharry, P. E., Ramig, L. O.
Title: Accurate Telemonitoring of Parkinson's Disease Progression by Noninvasive Speech Tests
Approach: Nonlinear speech metrics + linear and non-linear regression (random forests, lasso) predicting motor and total UPDRS scores
Accuracy_Metric: Mean Absolute Error 5.95 on motor-UPDRS, 7.52 on total-UPDRS
Limitations_Leakage_Risk: Longitudinal telemonitoring without healthy controls (progression only, not binary screening)
Notes: Establishes the telemonitoring progression benchmark based on home-recorded voice tests.

Title: Automatic detection of Parkinson's disease in running speech spoken in three different languages
Venue: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Approach: Voiced/unvoiced acoustic transition segmentation, MFCCs, Bark-band energies + SVM, Random Forest
Dataset: PC-GITA (Spanish), Czech, and German PD databases
Subjects: 88 Spanish (50 PD, 50 HC in full corpus), 50 Czech, 88 German
Accuracy_Metric: 84% to 99% depending on language and task
Limitations_Leakage_Risk: Continuous speech segmentation is sensitive to background ambient noise and dialectal variation
Notes: Demonstrates that articulatory and phonetic transitions in running speech generalize across languages.

Authors: Sakar, C. O., Serbes, G., Gunduz, A., Tunc, H. C., et al.
Title: A comparative analysis of speech signal processing algorithms for Parkinson's disease classification and the use of the tunable Q-factor wavelet transform
Approach: Tunable Q-factor Wavelet Transform (TQWT), MFCCs, time-frequency, baseline jitter/shimmer + ensemble classifiers
Accuracy_Metric: 86.0% Accuracy using TQWT features with SVM; ensemble reached ~89%
Limitations_Leakage_Risk: Large feature dimensionality (754 features) introduces risk of overfitting on modest subject cohorts
Notes: Introduced the popular UCI 470 dataset; established TQWT as a strong acoustic representation.

Authors: Alshammri, R., Alharbi, G., Alharbi, E., Almubark, I.
Title: Machine learning approaches to identify Parkinson's disease using voice signal features
Approach: SMOTE + feature selection + GridSearchCV on SVM, Random Forest, Decision Tree, KNN, MLP
Accuracy_Metric: MLP: 98.31% Accuracy, 99% F1; SVM: 95.0% Accuracy, 97% F1
Protocol: Random 70:30 train-test split (per recording, not grouped)
Limitations_Leakage_Risk: Severe data leakage: recordings from the same individual exist in both train and test sets, inflating metrics
Notes: Shows high claimed metrics on UCI dataset when subject grouping is neglected.

Authors: Pah, N. D., Indrawati, V., Kumar, D. K.
Title: Voice-Based SVM Model Reliability for Identifying Parkinson's Disease
Approach: Acoustic feature stability evaluation, variance analysis, support vector machine with linear and RBF kernels
Dataset: Multiple voice cohorts (including UCI and Italian PD Voice Database)
Accuracy_Metric: Accuracy 82.5% to 89.2% under repeated subject-isolated folds
Protocol: Subject-wise cross-validation with stability and reliability analysis
Limitations_Leakage_Risk: Demonstrates that sample-level splits drop significantly in accuracy when evaluated subject-wise
Notes: Crucial study highlighting the instability of voice-based SVMs when cross-validation ignores subject clustering.

Authors: Pah, N. D., Indrawati, V., Prayitno, A., Kumar, D. K.
Title: The Effectiveness of Acoustic Voice Quality Index to Identify People With Parkinson's Disease
Approach: Acoustic Voice Quality Index (AVQI) multiparametric dysphonia measure (smoothed cepstral peak, shimmer, jitter, HNR) + Logistic Regression / SVM
Dataset: Italian Parkinson Voice Database & benchmark corpora
Task_Type: Sustained vowel combined with continuous speech text
Limitations_Leakage_Risk: Requires calibrated recording microphones to match Praat AVQI normative thresholds accurately
Notes: Bridges sustained vowel phonation with continuous text sentences using clinical AVQI score.

Authors: Srinivasan, S., Rajasekar, R., et al.
Title: Detection of Parkinson disease using multiclass machine learning approach
Approach: Acoustic dysphonia parameters + SMOTE + RandomizedSearchCV hyperparameter optimization + FNN, KNN, KSVM
Limitations_Leakage_Risk: High risk of patient overlap across train and test sets due to per-sample split
Notes: Representative of recent deep learning / neural approaches achieving >95% without GroupKFold.

Authors: Ghaheri, P., Nasiri, H., Shateri, A., Homafar, A.
Title: Diagnosis of Parkinson's disease based on voice signals using SHAP and hard voting ensemble method
Venue: Computer Methods in Biomechanics and Biomedical Engineering
Approach: XGBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest, hard voting ensemble + SHAP (Shapley Additive exPlanations) for vocal biomarker importance
Accuracy_Metric: 96.55% Accuracy with voting ensemble; identified PPE and spread1 as top SHAP drivers
Limitations_Leakage_Risk: Lack of subject grouping allows tree ensembles to memorize subject-specific pitch signatures
Notes: Directly motivates our use of SHAP explainability and tree ensembles while highlighting the need for subject grouping.

Authors: La Quatra, M., Turco, M. F., Svendsen, T., Salvi, G., Orozco-Arroyave, J. R., Siniscalchi, S. M.
Title: Exploiting Foundation Models and Speech Enhancement for Parkinson's Disease Detection from Speech in Real-World Operative Conditions
Approach: Self-supervised speech foundation representations (Wav2Vec 2.0, HuBERT) + deep speech enhancement pre-processing
Dataset: PC-GITA Spanish corpus (clean and artificially corrupted with environmental noise)
Accuracy_Metric: Unweighted Average Recall (UAR) 83.2% in noisy real-world conditions
Limitations_Leakage_Risk: High computational footprint; requires heavy GPU inference compared to acoustic biomarkers
Notes: Validates that environmental noise dramatically degrades speech classifiers without front-end filtering.
